### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. autosomal dominant Kenny-Caffey syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.787)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:24725)

**Proposed mechanism:** FAM111A (HGNC:24725) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0000001); FAM111A (HGNC:24725) —LEADS_TO→ Cortical thickening of long bones (HP:0005907); FAM111A (HGNC:24725) —LEADS_TO→ Osteosclerosis (HP:0004471); FAM111A (HGNC:24725) —LEADS_TO→ Thickening of the bone cortex (HP:0005907); FAM111A (HGNC:24725) —LEADS_TO→ Severe short stature (HP:0004323); FAM111A (HGNC:24725) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital hypoparathyroidism (HP:0000870). Mutations in FAM111A lead to haploinsufficiency, causing a spectrum of skeletal abnormalities including osteosclerosis, cortical thickening of long bones, severe short stature, and congenital hypoparathyroidism, which are shared phenotypes between autosomal dominant Kenny-Caffey syndrome and the other disease.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in FAM111A with frequencies exceeding 0.1% in the general population (e.g., gnomAD) would challenge the hypothesis that FAM111A mutations are the primary cause of these diseases.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in FAM111A provides a unified target for potential therapeutic strategies aimed at ameliorating skeletal and endocrine manifestations in both conditions.
